description: Figure 4 (right panel) displays the performance of different activation editing methods on the BBQ benchmark, measured by Accuracy on the y-axis against the number of demonstrations (#Demonstrations) on the x-axis. The x-axis ranges from 0 to 1500 with tick marks at intervals of 250, and the y-axis ranges from 45 to 55 with tick marks at intervals of 5. Four methods are plotted: “Squared-Exponential” (solid dark blue line with circular markers), “Tanh” (solid medium blue line with circular markers), “ELU” (solid light purple line with circular markers), and “LLaMA-2-chat-7B” (dashed pink line with no markers). The “Squared-Exponential” method starts at approximately 53.5 accuracy at 0 demonstrations, rises slightly to ~55.5 by 250 demonstrations, and then plateaus near 55.5 through 1500 demonstrations. The “Tanh” method begins near 49.5, increases slightly to ~50 by 250, and remains stable around 50 through 1500. The “ELU” method starts near 47, rises slightly to ~48 by 250, and stays near 48 through 1500. The “LLaMA-2-chat-7B” baseline is a flat dashed pink line at approximately 47.5 across all demonstration counts. All three editing methods outperform the baseline, with “Squared-Exponential” achieving the highest accuracy.
